text.L1: Science is not just a list of facts to memorise. It is a way of finding out by observing, asking questions and testing ideas.
text.L2: Start by noticing something. Ask a question that you can answer by doing something and observing or measuring what happens.
text.L3: Before the test, make a prediction. It is a guess with a reason, based on what you already know.
text.L4: For example, ask whether curd sets faster in a warm place or a cool place. Predict that the warm bowl will set first because the starter bacteria work faster in warmth.
text.L5: Test fairly with the same milk, the same amount and the same starter. Keep one bowl warm and one bowl cool, then observe and record them after the same time.
text.L6: The result may support the prediction or may not. A wrong prediction is still useful because it teaches us something new and leads to another question.
text.L7: Remember the circle: observe, ask, predict, test and conclude. Then use what you learned to ask a new question.
